subject: Dedicated cluster sizing + phased ramp for BlueBridge - proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluebridge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nambiar <priya.nambiar@bluebridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated cluster

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited about Redwood’s latency profile, but procurement and engineering need a concrete sizing path tied to our Q1 rollout. I attached a quick usage estimate (see BlueBridge_MA_Modeling.xlsx) — it includes expected peak concurrent sessions and tokens per minute for the first 18 weeks.

High level ask: can you propose a minimal reservation that lets us guarantee 99th percentile latency <= 250ms for our baseline model while allowing a staged GPU ramp tied to our release milestones?

Also important: we need a plan for hot-standby burst and an explicit decommit/remediation window if traffic doesn’t materialize. Procurement would prefer clear milestone checkpoints for quarterly billing.

Appreciate a playbook we can take to our procurement team.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Product
BlueBridge AI

Attachment: BlueBridge_MA_Modeling.xlsx (xlsx, 124KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluebridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated cluster

Alex —

Thanks for the file — very helpful. I pulled the numbers into our capacity model and sketched three linked options you can present to procurement and engineering. Attached is a concise proposal (RBW-Dedicated-Offer-v3.pdf) plus the quick summary below.

Summary (short):
- Option A (Conservative): 16 GPUs reserved (min 12 active) — immediate availability. Guarantees 99th <= 220ms for baseline model at expected peak. Ramp: 0 -> 12 active over four weeks; optional +4 GPUs at week 12 if usage grows.
- Option B (Balanced): 12 GPUs reserved (min 8 active) — lower commit, higher burst credits. Guarantees 99th <= 250ms under typical peak; ramp: 0 -> 8 active in two weeks, staged increases at weeks 6 and 12 tied to milestone triggers.
- Option C (Cost-first): 8 GPUs reserved (min 4 active) — requires aggressive batching/prefix cache; 99th ~260–300ms at peak without caching optimization. Ramp: start with 4, review at week 6 for activation.

All options include: automated prefix caching, KV cache warming during rollouts, and model-variant fallback rules (smaller quantized variant automatically used if latency SLO is at risk). We modeled warmup credits for 14 days as part of the onboarding.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Engineering to pick target SLO (220 vs 250ms) — that will determine floor size.
2) Procurement to confirm milestone cadence (we propose week 4, 8, 12 checkpoints).
3) If you want, we can add an explicit decommit clause with gradual ramp-down and 30-day notification window.

I’m looping in Karthik for the activation timeline and Marissa for finance/billing cadence.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RBW-Dedicated-Offer-v3.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Priya Nambiar <priya.nambiar@bluebridge.ai>

Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluebridge.ai>, procurement@bluebridge.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated cluster

Irene/Karthik —

Quick procurement questions before we share with legal:
1) Can you confirm whether "min GPUs active" is billed while idle or only when nodes are spun up? We need clarity for our cash flows.
2) For Option A, what are the SLA credits if 99th jumps above 250ms for two consecutive days?
3) Do you offer a 60‑day pilot with pro‑rated credits applied to an annual commitment?

If you can answer inline that would be great. We’ll aim to get legal engaged next week.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Nambiar
Head of Procurement
BlueBridge AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Nambiar <priya.nambiar@bluebridge.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluebridge.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated cluster

Priya —

Answers inline:
1) Billing for "min GPUs active": our standard reserved model charges the reservation fee for the committed GPUs (the floor) irrespective of utilization — that secures capacity and warm caches. Operational burst above the floor is billed at a reduced burst rate. We can structure trials with warmup credits to reduce first‑month impact.
2) SLA credits: for persistent 99th violations (>250ms) over a 48hr rolling window we offer tiered credits — 5% credit for first 48hr window, escalating to 15% if unresolved for 7 days while we provide remediation (root cause & mitigation). We include automatic fallback to a lower‑latency variant while remediation is ongoing.
3) 60‑day pilot: yes, we can do a pilot. Typical structure: 60‑day pilot with 50% credits applied to the first year of a 12‑month commitment if BlueBridge converts within 90 days of pilot end. That would be inserted into the commercial term sheet.

Operational notes: onboarding will include a 10‑day KV cache warm period (we recommend traffic‑directed warmup windows) and an initial prewarming plan coordinated with your release windows. For large bursts we recommend a 20% surge buffer in the first 8 weeks.

Happy to jump on a call to align milestones with procurement and engineering.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluebridge.ai>, Priya Nambiar <priya.nambiar@bluebridge.ai>, procurement@bluebridge.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated cluster

Team —

Based on your procurement asks and the modeling, here is a recommended booking that balances performance and cash impact:

Recommended (final):
- Commit: 12 GPUs reserved (billed as floor) with min active = 8 for first 12 weeks.
- Ramp schedule: Weeks 0–2: bring 4 GPUs online for smoke tests and KV warmup; Weeks 3–6: scale to 8 active; Week 12: automatic activation to 12 active if cumulative peak > 75th percentile for 3 consecutive days (or earlier by mutual consent).
- Burst: additional on-demand burst pool up to +50% of committed GPUs billed at burst rate.
- Pilot clause: 60‑day pilot with 50% pilot credits applied pro‑rata to month 1 of the annual commit if converted.
- SLA/remediation: tiered credits as outlined by Karthik; automatic model fallback and operational runbook for traffic surges.
- Decommit: 90‑day notice window for stepdown of reserved floor; partial decommit allowed at quarter boundaries with a 30% step penalty if decommit happens within first 180 days.

Attached is a short summary you can hand to legal and procurement. If that aligns, we’ll prepare the commercial term sheet and a more detailed activation playbook (onboarding calendar + runbook).

Would you like a 30‑minute sync Friday to walk through milestones?

Best,
Irene
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RBW-Dedicated-Offer-v3.pdf (updated summary)
